key_insight: Learning test-time ensemble weights depends on two sample sizes, and buffered ERM achieves near-optimal excess risk of order Q^{-1/2}+N^{-β/2} under a margin condition.
engineering_relevance: For LLM ensembling, this gives a practical scaling law for how many labeled questions (Q) and generations per model (N) are needed to improve voting-based test-time performance.
method: Buffered ERM adds a calibrated margin buffer to stabilize weight learning.
A simplified two-model/two-answer submodel is used to derive minimax lower bounds.
Hellinger-modulus, polynomial approximation, and spectral analysis expose three sample-size regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical excess-risk bounds and minimax characterizations, rather than empirical experiments, with rates depending on Q, N, and the margin exponent β.
watch_item: The sharp transitions between the identified regimes are not fully resolved, and a matching pooled estimator for general ensembles is still open.
paper_title: Two Sample Sizes in Test-Time LLM Ensembling: Buffered ERM and Minimax Theory
